subject: SNP table - How to code for for missing data

messages.author: 752aaa009ee55b1c
messages.subject: SNP table - How to code for for missing data
parts:
Dear POPPRers,

I am new here and getting ready to use this amazing package! I am dealing with an organism with alternate reproduction, and I want to perform clone correction on SNP data.  Right now, I have a table with loci on columns and  genotypes coded as A/A G/G etc. I have not imported the table in POPPR yet, but I am not sure how I should code for missing data. Right now I just have them as "N" . Also, I understand I will have to remove the "/" before importing (e.g.: A/A --> AA). Can you please advice?

Cheers,
Max

messages.author: d192ec4b1d416345
messages.subject: Re: [poppr] SNP table - How to code for for missing data
parts:
Hi Max,

You shouldn't need to remove the "/" from the genotypes. When you import your data with df2genind(), you can specify sep = "/", and it will detect it.

Additionally, if you code the "N" as "NA", then you should be able to import them just fine since that's how R recognizes missing data.

Hope that helps,
Zhian
